home.heroSubtitle: Split's largest beach, reimagined — your complete guide to the Miami of Split
home.beachAreasSubtitle: Discover the different zones of Žnjan Beach
home.storyText1: What was once a neglected stretch of coastline is now Split's crown jewel. The €45.77M transformation brought world-class infrastructure, a palm-lined promenade, and 11 brand-new pavilion venues to life.
home.storyText2: From sunrise coffee at Central Beach to sunset cocktails at Taboo — Žnjan's new pavilion restaurants serve fresh Dalmatian cuisine with Adriatic views. Seven venues, each with its own character.
home.storyText3: Paddleboard at dawn, volleyball at noon, and live music at dusk. With a 1,200m² skate park, children's playground, and amphitheater with a steel dome, there's always something happening.
home.instagramSubtitle: See what awaits you at the beach

community.startTitle: Join the pilot in one useful move
community.startDescription: You do not need to master the whole system today. Check a court, join a meetup, or send one real signal so the public pilot gets better this week.
community.startActionsDescription: Three low-friction ways to help the system feel alive, trustworthy, and worth repeating.
community.startActionScheduleBody: Use the public sports access page first. It clearly explains that all sports areas are free, public, and first-come, first-served.
community.startActionMeetupsBody: Browse open meetups if you want people, not just a slot. This is where the first community layer becomes visible.
community.startActionFeedbackBody: If something is confusing, broken, or worth improving, send it in. Honest signal is more useful than quiet frustration.
community.startWhoDescription: This page is built for the first real wave of locals, helpers, and regulars.
community.startWhoPoint1: Beach regulars who want a simpler way to check courts and find people.
community.startWhoPoint2: Locals who can join one early meetup and help the community feed stop feeling empty.
community.startWhoPoint3: Helpers, venue staff, and friends who can show someone the public flow without improvising a private explanation.
community.startFlowTitle: How the first meetup wave works
community.startFlowDescription: Keep the first wave small, visible, and human. The goal is not scale yet. The goal is a believable rhythm.
community.startFlowPoint1: Pick one meetup that is easy to explain in one sentence and easy to find on site.
community.startFlowPoint2: Show the public rules and quick-start page first so everyone enters through the same honest flow.
community.startFlowPoint3: After the meetup, leave one useful post or piece of feedback so the next person sees momentum instead of silence.
community.startFinalDescription: Znjan.com does not need everyone to do everything. One sports-access check, one meetup, one report, or one helpful introduction is enough to move the project forward.
community.pilotUpdateTitle: What is live at Znjan right now
community.pilotUpdateDescription: A short honest update on the public sports access and community effort: what is clear today, what is not being promised, and where locals can help this week.
community.pilotUpdateFounderNote: This remains a volunteer civic project. The goal is public usefulness first, polish second, and transparency throughout.
community.pilotUpdateNowPoint1: Clear public guidance that all sports activities are free and there is no current reservation system for the beach sports areas.
community.pilotUpdateNowPoint2: Public pages, QR materials, and simple rules explaining that the courts and activity areas are first-come, first-served.
community.pilotUpdateNowPoint3: An early community layer for meetups, sports-partner posts, pilot feedback, and founder-led local invites.
community.pilotUpdateNotPoint1: It is not legal control over public beach spaces or a claim that the courts belong to the platform.
community.pilotUpdateNotPoint2: It is not a fully staffed support operation with formal on-site coverage every hour of the day.
community.pilotUpdateNotPoint3: It is not the finished commercial or mobile ecosystem yet. The current focus is proving public utility honestly.
community.pilotUpdateHelpPoint1: Share the sports access page before walking onto a court so people know the areas are free, public, and not bookable.
community.pilotUpdateHelpPoint2: Join one meetup, create one simple local session, or bring one real person into the public flow.
community.pilotUpdateHelpPoint3: Report conflicts or confusing moments so the system improves in public instead of drifting into guesswork.
community.pilotUpdateFinalTitle: If you share one link, share this one
community.pilotUpdateFinalDescription: Use this page as the short public explanation for friends, helpers, venues, and early supporters. Then send people to the start page, the sports access page, or contact depending on what they need.
community.helpTitle: Help Znjan.com in one concrete way this week
community.helpDescription: This is a volunteer civic project. The most useful support is simple: bring one person into the public flow, share one honest page, or send one real signal that improves the pilot.
community.helpCardsTitle: Choose the kind of help that fits you
community.helpCardsDescription: Different people can help in different ways. Pick the one that matches what you can actually do this week.
community.helpCardLocalTitle: Bring one local into the public flow
community.helpCardLocalBody: Send one friend or beach regular to the start page so they enter through the same honest sports-access, meetup, and feedback path.
community.helpCardShareBody: Use the public pilot page when you want to explain what is live now without hype, confusion, or private backstory.
community.helpCardOnSiteTitle: Use the quick-start page on site
community.helpCardOnSiteBody: If someone asks what to do at the courts or sessions, show them the same public quick-start flow instead of improvising from memory.
community.helpCardSignalBody: If something is confusing, conflicting, or worth fixing, report it. Honest signal is more useful than silent frustration.
community.helpWhoDescription: You do not need a formal role to be useful. The early pilot works because regular people do small clear things consistently.
community.helpWhoPoint1: Locals who can explain that the sports areas are public, free, and first-come, first-served.
community.helpWhoPoint2: Friends or helpers who can show one person the start or quick-start page without inventing a private explanation.
community.helpWhoPoint3: Venue staff or beach regulars who can pass along one honest public link when someone asks what this is.
community.helpWhoPoint4: Early supporters who can share the public update calmly instead of over-promising what the project is not yet.
community.helpStepsDescription: If you want the shortest version, do one of these and the pilot is already stronger.
community.helpStep1: Before using a court or activity area, read the sports access note and follow any official on-site signage.
community.helpStep2: Join one meetup or create one simple local session if you already know the people who should be there.
community.helpStep3: Share the public pilot update or the start page with one person who is actually likely to use it.
community.helpStep4: Report one confusing or conflicting moment so the system improves in public instead of drifting into guesswork.
community.helpSignalTitle: Raise your hand if you can help
community.helpSignalDescription: This is the lightweight intake for people who can actually help the pilot. It is for concrete support, not abstract encouragement.
community.helpSignalPoint1: Use this if you can introduce real locals, help on site, connect a venue, or send grounded pilot feedback.
community.helpSignalPoint2: You do not need a formal title. Short honest signals are more useful than over-committed promises.
community.helpSignalPoint3: The founder will use these signals to decide who to follow up with for the next weekends and meetups.
community.helpSignalFormDescription: Leave one concrete note so the founder can turn willing support into actual next steps.
community.helpSignalType: What kind of support is this?
community.helpSignalTypeVenue: I can connect a venue or staff contact
community.helpSignalNamePlaceholder: Example: Ivan, Ana, regular volleyball player, or pavilion staff member
community.helpSignalContactPlaceholder: Email, Instagram handle, WhatsApp number, or other contact you actually check
community.helpSignalAvailabilityPlaceholder: Optional: this weekend afternoons, usually near volleyball courts, work at one of the pavilions
community.helpSignalNotesPlaceholder: Be concrete: what you can do, who you can introduce, what you noticed, or what kind of follow-up would help.
community.helpSignalRuleNote: Only send signals you actually mean. Specific honest help is much better than vague enthusiasm.
community.helpSignalSuccess: Thanks — your support signal was sent.
community.helpSignalError: Something went wrong while sending your signal. Please try again.
community.helpFinalTitle: This works best when the help stays honest
community.helpFinalDescription: The project does not need hype, inflated promises, or private workarounds. It needs visible public use, clear links, and real feedback.

reservations.title: Sports Access
reservations.subtitle: All public sports activities at Žnjan are free to use. There is no current reservation system, and the beach sports areas are open on a first-come, first-served basis.
reservations.rulesPageTitle: How sports access works at Žnjan
reservations.rulesPageDescription: The sports areas are free, public, and currently work without a reservation system. Here is the clearest current note for visitors and locals.
reservations.ruleFree: All public sports activities at Žnjan are free.
reservations.ruleWindow: There is no current reservation system for the beach sports areas.
reservations.ruleDuration: Courts and activity areas are public spaces, not bookable time slots.
reservations.ruleDailyLimit: Use works on a first-come, first-served basis.
reservations.ruleCancellation: No booking or cancellation is required.
reservations.ruleNoShow: Share the space fairly, especially when others are already waiting on site.
reservations.rulePublic: Any official on-site signage or closures takes priority.
reservations.trustNoteBody: Znjan.com does not operate a current reservation system for the sports areas. These pages exist to set clear expectations: the courts and activity areas are public, free, and first-come, first-served.
reservations.trustPointCoordination: All public sports activities at Žnjan are currently free to use.
reservations.trustPointPrivacy: No sign-in is required to use the public sports areas.
reservations.trustPointReport: If official signage or access rules change on site, contact us so we can update the website quickly.
reservations.quickStartDescription: Use this page when you scan a sticker or pick up a flyer at the beach. It explains the current reality simply: all sports areas are free, public, and first-come, first-served.

reservations.quickStartStep1: Pick the court or activity area you want to use.
reservations.quickStartStep2: All public sports activities are free and there is no current reservation system.
reservations.quickStartStep3: The sports areas are open to everyone on a first-come, first-served basis.
reservations.quickStartStep4: If official signs, closures, or operating rules change on site, check this page or contact the team.
reservations.quickStartPilotResourcesBody: Beach volleyball, tennis, basketball, cage football, skate park, and promenade fitness remain public sports areas.
reservations.quickStartOpenTodayBody: No fees apply to the public sports areas.
reservations.quickStartWindowBody: There is no booking window because there is no current reservation system.
reservations.quickStartOnSiteTitle: For QR stickers, flyers, and beach handouts
reservations.quickStartOnSiteBody: Share this page whenever someone asks whether the courts or sports areas can be booked. Right now they cannot.
reservations.pilotKitDescription: Print-ready material for the public sports access message. Use it to share one clear truth: all sports activities are free, there is no current reservation system, and the sports areas are first-come, first-served.

reservations.pilotKitFlyerBody: All public sports areas are open to everyone. There is no current reservation system.
reservations.pilotKitPosterBody: Scan here for the current sports access note. All public sports activities are free, and the areas work on a first-come, first-served basis.
reservations.pilotKitUsagePoint1: Place QR stickers where people are deciding whether a court or sports area is free to use.
reservations.pilotKitUsagePoint2: Use flyers and table cards in pavilions, bars, and restaurants that want to share clear public information.
reservations.pilotKitUsagePoint3: Do not describe this as a booking system. Describe it as a public access note for shared beach sports areas.
reservations.pilotKitSupportPoint1: Confirm the quick-start page, sports access page, and contact page all load on your phone.
reservations.pilotKitSupportPoint2: Make sure the message about free public use and first-come, first-served access is still clear.
reservations.pilotKitSupportPoint3: If official on-site rules change, update the website before handing out more materials.

reservations.pilotFutureBody: If the city or official operators publish new access rules in future, Znjan.com will update these pages.

reservations.fairnessPointClosures: If an area is officially closed or posted with temporary rules on site, follow that guidance first.

admin.commercialSellNowPoint1: Verified place page and directory presence on Znjan.com.
admin.commercialSellNowPoint2: Featured placement on existing web surfaces such as key listings or manually curated highlight sections.
admin.commercialSellNowPoint3: Web-first event or announcement visibility tied to pages that are already live.
admin.commercialSellNowPoint4: Founder-led pilot storytelling or public update mentions when it fits the civic scope of the project.

admin.commercialPromptsDescription: Simple founder questions that help you validate demand before building product sprawl.
admin.commercialPrompt1: If Znjan.com could help one thing for your venue this summer, what would actually matter enough for you to pay attention?
admin.commercialPrompt2: Would a verified page, featured web placement, or event visibility be more useful than generic social promotion?
admin.commercialPrompt3: What would you need to see on the live site before taking a paid or pilot step with us?
admin.commercialSellSheetDescription: A lightweight founder-ready offer sheet for honest Summer 2026 venue conversations, based only on web surfaces that already exist.
admin.commercialSellSheetHeroTitle: What Znjan.com can honestly offer venues right now
admin.commercialSellSheetHeroBody: Znjan.com is already live as a multilingual civic guide, a public sports-access information surface, and a public update layer for Znjan Beach. This sheet is for simple Summer 2026 conversations with venues that want visibility on channels that already exist today.
admin.commercialSellSheetWhatExistsDescription: Use this section to show venues that the project is already real, public, and useful before any heavier commercial tooling is built.
admin.commercialSellSheetOffersDescription: Keep the initial commercial offer narrow, web-first, and grounded in surfaces that are already visible on znjan.com.
admin.commercialSellSheetOfferVerifiedBody: A verified venue page on Znjan.com with accurate public information, clear positioning, and multilingual discovery value.
admin.commercialSellSheetOfferFeatureBody: Extra visibility on existing web surfaces such as highlighted listings, homepage modules, or founder-curated placement where it genuinely fits.
admin.commercialSellSheetOfferEventBody: Web-first promotion for a venue event, activation, or timely announcement through live pages the public can actually visit now.
admin.commercialSellSheetOfferStoryBody: Selective inclusion in founder updates or pilot storytelling when the venue genuinely helps the public-service layer grow.
admin.commercialSellSheetPromptsDescription: Use these questions to validate demand before promising product work. The goal is clarity, not over-selling.
admin.commercialSellSheetNotYetDescription: This is the boundary that keeps the commercial story honest. If the surface is not live yet, it should not be sold as if it is.
admin.commercialSellSheetHowToUseDescription: Treat this as a founder tool for real conversations, not a polished agency deck.
admin.commercialSellSheetHowToUsePoint1: Open with the public pilot page or places directory so the venue sees a real live product first.
admin.commercialSellSheetHowToUsePoint2: Keep the offer to one or two web surfaces that fit the venue instead of pitching a bundle by default.
admin.commercialSellSheetHowToUsePoint3: Log the outcome back in the venue-validation page the same day so demand signals stay measurable.
admin.commercialSellSheetPrintDescription: A print-friendly one-page version of the founder sell sheet with live proof links and QR codes for venue conversations.
admin.commercialSellSheetPrintHeroTitle: One-page venue sheet for real Summer 2026 conversations
admin.commercialSellSheetPrintHeroBody: Use this as a simple leave-behind or table sheet during pavilion walks. It stays grounded in live public surfaces, shows what exists today, and gives venues two QR paths into the real product.
admin.commercialSellSheetPrintQrBody: These codes open real public surfaces the venue can check immediately on their own phone.
admin.commercialSellSheetPrintNotesDescription: Use these lines for decision-maker notes, follow-up timing, pricing reactions, or next-step commitments.
admin.commsDescription: A founder-ready messaging kit for the first public posts, venue follow-ups, supporter shares, and honest civic framing during the pilot.
admin.commsOneLineDescription: Use this when someone asks what Znjan.com is before they want the full story.
admin.commsOneLineBody: Znjan.com is a multilingual civic guide and public coordination project for Znjan Beach, helping people discover the beach, understand how the public sports areas work, and stay aligned around the same clear rules.
admin.commsBioDescription: Short reusable profile text for channels, group descriptions, and link pages.
admin.commsBioShortText: Public guide + sports access updates for Znjan Beach. Local meetups and honest updates from Split's beach community.
admin.commsBioLongText: Znjan.com is building a public, multilingual guide and community coordination layer for Znjan Beach in Split. Check the sports access pages, follow honest public updates, and join early local meetups.
admin.commsDirectDescription: Use these when messaging a venue, helper, or early supporter who needs a simple introduction.
admin.commsDirectVenueText: Hi, I'm building a volunteer civic project for Znjan that helps people understand the public sports areas clearly and keeps the public message honest. This page explains what is already live and how it works:
admin.commsDirectSupporterText: Hi, this is the shortest honest update on the Znjan pilot right now. If you want to share one link with locals or friends, use this one first:
admin.commsPostsDescription: Three simple narratives for the first wave of posts, Stories, WhatsApp shares, or supporter forwards.
admin.commsCadenceDescription: A simple founder rhythm for the first public week so the narrative stays consistent across posts, forwards, and venue follow-ups.
admin.commsCadenceStep1Title: Lead with the public pilot update
admin.commsCadenceStep1Body: Start with the shortest honest explanation of what is live now. This is the safest opener for supporters, venues, and local friends because it sets expectations before asking for action.
admin.commsCadenceStep2Title: Send locals to the start page
admin.commsCadenceStep2Body: After people understand the pilot, point them to the start page so they can choose one useful action instead of bouncing off the raw feed or guessing where to begin.
admin.commsCadenceStep3Title: Use the quick-start page on site
admin.commsCadenceStep3Body: When a QR sticker, flyer, or handout is involved, switch to the quick-start route. It is the cleanest entry point for people who are already standing at Znjan.
admin.commsCadenceStep4Title: Close the loop with public metrics
admin.commsCadenceStep4Body: Follow up with the transparency dashboard once people have seen the system. This keeps the project grounded in public evidence instead of vague claims.
admin.commsPostLiveBody: Znjan now has a clear public sports-access information layer with public rules, transparent updates, and one honest message: the sports areas are free, open to the public, and first-come, first-served.
admin.commsPostStartBody: If you're local and want the easiest way in, start here: check today's schedule, browse the first meetups, or send one useful piece of feedback. You do not need to learn the whole system in one day.
admin.commsPostPlayTitle: Post 3: For people already at the beach
admin.commsPostPlayBody: If you see a QR sticker or get a flyer at Znjan, use the quick-start page. It takes you straight to the sports access note, the current rules, and the latest public update without overcomplicating the first step.
admin.commsAssetsDescription: Use the public page URL when you want people to click through. Use the social-card URL when you need a clean preview image for a post, Story, or supporter handoff.
admin.commsGuardrailsDescription: Keep public language useful, calm, and honest.
admin.commsGuardrail1: Do not describe the platform as legal control over public courts or activity areas.
admin.commsGuardrail2: Do not promise full staffing, guaranteed enforcement, or perfect real-time accuracy on site.
admin.commsGuardrail3: Always point people back to the public rules, start page, or dashboard instead of inventing private exceptions.
admin.commsGuardrail4: Keep the tone civic and practical. This works better than startup hype for this project.
admin.seedCommunityDescription: Founder tools for inviting the first locals, scheduling the first 3 meetups, and giving helpers a simple, repeatable script.
admin.seedInviteDescription: Keep the first wave manual and personal so the community starts with real people, not random traffic.
admin.seedInvitePoint1: Invite people you already know from Žnjan, Split sports circles, nearby neighborhoods, and trusted regulars.
admin.seedInvitePoint2: Each invite should ask for one clear action: create an account, join a meetup, or give pilot feedback.
admin.seedInvitePoint3: Track who already joined so follow-ups stay respectful instead of spammy.
admin.seedInvitePoint4: If someone is real and helpful but not yet active, use founder trust manually before you build heavier systems.
admin.seedMeetupTemplatesDescription: These are lightweight founder templates for the first 3 meetups. Open one, adjust details, and publish only when the timing really works.
admin.seedTemplateVolleyballDescription: Open morning volleyball for early beach regulars. Use this to make the first sports meetup easy to join and easy to explain.
admin.seedTemplateTennisDescription: A simple tennis meetup for locals looking for a rally partner and a first reason to try the community flow.
admin.seedTemplateSunsetDescription: A low-pressure social meetup on the promenade to gather locals, hear what feels confusing, and build early trust.
admin.seedHelperDescription: Use a lightweight helper model first. The goal is not formal staffing yet, but reliable coverage and calm human support.
admin.seedHelperPoint1: Ask helpers to show people the quick-start page and the public rules before answering from memory.
admin.seedHelperPoint2: If a conflict happens, helpers should direct the person to the public path first and log details through the admin tools the same day.
admin.seedHelperPoint3: Keep coverage windows small and explicit so the first 2 weekends feel dependable without overpromising.
admin.seedSupportSignalsDescription: Structured signals from the public help page so founder follow-up does not depend on scattered DMs.
